factual_methodology.summary: Checked WHO 2020–21 excess mortality definition and estimated toll, WHO 2026 post-COVID risk and the October 12 UN pandemic declaration; distinguished estimates from observed totals and political declarations from implemented preparedness.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Links mortality, work, schooling, psychosocial impacts, access to care and institutional readiness through mechanisms rather than treating the pandemic as a GDP-only event.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Source-linked quantitative charts, evidence tables, causal flow and scoped maps in both locales; 2 chart(s), 1 flow(s), 1 map(s).

research_depth.summary: Links mortality, work, schooling, psychosocial impacts, access to care and institutional readiness through mechanisms rather than treating the pandemic as a GDP-only event.

evidence_traceability.summary: Twenty-three distinct institutional and academic references in each locale, including WHO, ILO, UNESCO, OECD, IMF, World Bank and CEPI; historical figures and 2026 policy status are attributed and limitations stated.

counterfactual_review.summary: Examines alternative explanations for learning and mental health changes, heterogeneity of pathogens and intervention effects, unequal social exposure, and conditional response scenarios.

contrary_evidence: Excess mortality estimates include indirect causes and are not interchangeable with confirmed disease-specific deaths.
Psychosocial outcomes and learning changes have confounders; they cannot all be attributed to isolation policies.
Future outbreaks need not resemble SARS-CoV-2, and no evidence establishes a specific future pandemic timing.
limitations: This review confirms principal institutional anchor facts and bilingual structure; it does not constitute external peer review of every cited study.
Historical estimated burdens and current clinical surveillance use different periods and denominators.
The Pandemic Agreement and PABS negotiations are not equivalent to fully implemented international preparedness.
notes: Internal documentary and bilingual QA with manual checks against selected institutional primary sources and deterministic structure/visual parity; not external scientific peer review. Targeted final factual-neutral prose fixes: English self-reference removed; Portuguese vaccine manufacturing quality control terminology clarified.
